Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the chase to commence. The two openers of West Indies, Kraigg Brathwaite and Mikyle Louis have made their way out to the middle. Hasan Mahmud will start with the new ball for Bangladesh. Here we go!
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

Jaker fell 9 runs short of a hundred, but he has well and truly ramped home the advantage for the tourists by taking them to a lead of 286 runs. Only twice have scores of 200-plus been successfully chased at this venue in Tests, with the highest being 212. This highlights the monumental task that lies ahead for the West Indies' batters, who will be low on confidence after being bowled out for just 146. With the remaining time in the current session and five more sessions to follow, time is not an issue for the hosts. While it's not an impossible task, they will have to bat out of their skins to gun down this total.

End of an exceptional knock from Jaker Ali, and that draws the curtains on Bangladesh's second innings. They have managed to add 75 runs to their overnight score for the loss of 5 wickets, ending up with a lead of 286 runs. Starting the day with a lead of 211 runs, Jaker Ali and Taijul Islam went about their business quietly, but the change in the ball brought immediate success as Alzarri Joseph and Kemar Roach struck in quick succession. Jaker trusted Hasan Mahmud and Taskin Ahmed, not farming the strike which many believed he should have. He lost both of them and with only one wicket left, he began farming the strike and went into overdrive. Whether it was the short ball or any other length, he dispatched them with equal disdain, frustrating the hosts in the process.

Justin Greaves is in for a chat. He starts by saying that they as a bowling group need to be disciplined. Further adds that the pitch is still looking good. PITCH REPORT - Nikhil Uttamchandani is near the deck. He informs that 200-plus totals have only been successfully chased twice in Test cricket at this venue. Samuel Badree joins him and highlights that the cracks on the pitch have opened up significantly, posing a stern challenge for the batters. He adds that both pacers and spinners will have a crucial role to play. Badree mentions that some deliveries from spinners turned sharply yesterday while others held their line, making it a true test of the batters’ skills.

With 212 being the highest successful run chase in Tests at Sabina Park, this total is already pushing the Windies into challenging territory. Bangladesh will hope Mominul Haque, who missed action on Day 3 due to illness, recovers enough to contribute on Day 4. Play will start early once again, with the first ball scheduled for 2.45 pm GMT. Stay tuned!

Bangladesh capitalised on a narrow first-innings lead of 18 runs, finishing Day 3 at 193/5, extending their advantage. Shadman Islam and Mehidy Hasan led the charge with attacking, confident batting to stretch the lead. Mehidy’s intent-laden strokes during his stay were particularly eye-catching. Nahid Rana’s dominant maiden Test five-wicket haul, running in with high intensity and pace, had earlier broken West Indies’ resolve. With a firm 211-run lead and five wickets in hand, Bangladesh are in a commanding position, though the West Indies will be keen to fight back hard.

Starting Day 3 at 70/1, West Indies were in a decent position but endured a dramatic collapse, eventually being bowled out for a modest 146. Despite a strong start, they lost their final nine wickets for just 61 runs. West Indies' troubles were compounded with fast bowler Kemar Roach sidelined for much of the day, having sustained blows to his left shoulder while batting. The hosts also had fielding lapses, notably dropping a crucial catch of Litton Das in the second innings, though it did not cost them a lot. They will have to hold onto their chances if they are to take the remaining wickets quickly.

Hello and welcome to Day 4 of the second Test between the West Indies and Bangladesh. We are set for another intriguing day of cricket. Day 3 was a topsy-turvy affair that started with West Indies on top, but by the end of it, Bangladesh took the ascendancy. The weather forecast predicts mostly sunny conditions with a few clouds, creating a perfect setting for the game to progress. The pitch is expected to assist the seamers, particularly early in the day, but whether it eases out as it did through sessions 2 and 3 on Day 3 remains to be seen. With both teams striving for victory, this day promises to deliver more twists in a tightly contested encounter.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

With 212 being the highest successful run chase at this venue in Tests, the Windies already have a mountain to climb in terms of their batting. However, the positive for them is that batting seemed to get easier when Bangladesh batted, with the lateral movement not as pronounced as it was in the first innings. For Bangladesh, they will be hoping to bat for as long as possible to set an even more challenging target. A key factor for them will be the fitness of Mominul Haque, whom we did spot being padded up, though he did not look visibly well. Due to the time lost on the opening day, we will have an early start on Day 4 as well, with the first ball to be bowled at 2.45 pm GMT. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Andre Adams, the bowling coach of Bangladesh is in for a quick chat with Ian Bishop. He says that it was a very good day and the boys showed some fight. Talking about Nahid Rana, he mentions that the wickets are going to come to him when you bowl at that pace. Further adds that his workload was being managed in the first Test and that was the reason he didn't play. Talking about the situation of the game, he says that firstly they have to put up more runs on the board and then look to bowl well in the last innings.

The Windies were also dealing with their own absentee, as Kemar Roach had been off the field after taking a couple of blows to his left shoulder while batting and was sent for an X-ray. His absence was felt keenly, but the hosts found some inspiration through Shamar Joseph, who removed both set batters early in the third session. Despite that, they could not run through the rest of the batting unit as they might have hoped, and the runs continued to leak. They managed to gain control with the departure of Litton Das and the return of Roach for a 5-over spell. However, the resilience from Bangladesh shone through as the pair of Jaker Ali and Taijul Islam held firm, guiding them to the end of the day with a lead of 211 runs.

Bangladesh’s second innings began under intense conditions, with a lot of chatter around the bat, so much so that the umpires had to intervene several times. A fired-up Jayden Seales was in the thick of it, claiming the wicket of Mahmudul Hasan Joy in the very first over. However, Shahadat Hossain stepped up with a counter-attacking innings that quietened the chatter. In the absence of Mominul Haque, who did not take the field due to illness, Mehidy Hasan promoted himself up the order and kept the momentum going alongside Shadman Islam.

Well, it’s called the 'moving day' for a reason, isn’t it? At the start of play, the West Indies seemed to have the upper hand at 70/1 in response to Bangladesh's 164. However, by the close of the day, that balance of power has shifted firmly towards the visitors. Kraigg Brathwaite and Keacy Carty began the day cautiously, but the pivotal moment came when Brathwaite was dismissed by a sharp bouncer from Nahid Rana. That sparked a dramatic collapse, with Rana leading the charge, claiming his maiden Test five-wicket haul. The West Indies fell from a solid 85/1 to 146 all out, handing Bangladesh an 18-run lead.

Shadman Islam and Mehidy Hasan followed suit, adopting a positive approach to keep the scoreboard moving. Their unbeaten 63-run stand ensured a productive session for Bangladesh, helping them stretch the lead to 128 runs. The West Indies have clearly felt the absence of Kemar Roach, who has gone for an X-ray after sustaining a couple of blows to his left shoulder while batting. They will need inspiration in the third session to claw their way back into the game and will be hoping for Roach’s return to bolster their attack. Back in a bit for the third session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 23 overs, 121 runs and 4 wickets. The second session in a row has gone in favour of Bangladesh. After dominating with the ball earlier, they have carried the momentum into their batting, scoring at an impressive rate of 5.5 runs per over. Having wrapped up the West Indies' innings quickly in just three overs after the Lunch break, the visitors gained an 18-run lead. The intensity was palpable from the start, with plenty of chatter around the bat even before a ball was bowled. When Mahmudul Hasan Joy fell to Jayden Seales in the very first over, the West Indies were buzzing. However, Shahadat Hossain, coming in at number three, countered with intent-laden strokes, putting the pressure back on the hosts.
